prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The bright hands, turquoise cloth, and thread are the nearest surfaces, roughly 0.3–0.6 m from the camera, above the orange-clad lap; the ground, rocks, yellow mat, and small turquoise bundle lie farther away, approximately 0.8–2 m. The depth layers clarify that the hands overlap the cloth and torso, while the thread extends rightward at about hand depth before crossing more distant ground. Across the five frames the near person remains at nearly constant range while the view shifts slightly right; in frame 5, a partly cropped arm and blue object enter from the right at roughly 0.5–1 m. Absolute distances are uncertain, and depth around thin thread, fingers, object edges, and the far-right entrant is visibly smeared or incomplete.
descriptions.segmentation: The map consistently isolates a large person region occupying the lower-middle foreground, corresponding to the orange-clad body and hands directly in front of and below the camera; a bed-like region is labeled in frame 2 behind and to the left/upper side of that person. It makes the foreground person's broad extent and occlusion of the ground easier to see than in RGB, including the body continuing beyond the bottom edge and the arms overlapping the torso. A second person label appears only at the extreme right of frame 5, indicating someone mostly outside the view and roughly beside the foreground person, although the mask does not provide metric distance or facing direction. The masks fluctuate substantially between frames, merge clothing, hands, and nearby surfaces, and omit or misclassify the turquoise cloth, thread, rocks, mat, and other small objects, so fine spatial boundaries and changes are unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The magenta hand skeletons place both hands close together in the lower-left-to-central foreground, roughly 0.3–0.5 m from the camera and within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, with one hand generally left of the other and both above the turquoise cloth/lap. Their orientation shows fingers directed inward toward the cloth and partially toward each other; no body skeleton, head, gaze, or face is detected, so the map cannot establish which way any person faces or whether anyone looks toward the camera. Across frames 1–2 the two hand poses remain similar, frame 3 retains mainly the right-side hand, frame 4 loses both detections, and frame 5 restores two hands farther right in the image as the viewpoint shifts. The skeleton map exposes finger placement that is hard to separate in RGB, but missing joints, frame-to-frame dropouts, overlapping fingers, and the absence of the partly visible person at the far right make it unreliable for complete reach, occlusion, or person-to-person geometry.
